description: Thermal domain example: a DC motor whose copper loss heats its winding, which conducts to the housing, which cools by convection. The steady state is the fixed point of the electro-thermal loop (speed, current and loss depend on R(T_winding)); the first-law checks hold at every sample.

checks.note: fixed point: R = R0*(1 + alpha*(Tw - T_ref)), w = k*V/(k^2 + R*d), i = d*w/k, P = R*i^2, Th = Ta + P/(h*A), Tw = Th + P/G_ins; 2400 s is about 13 slow time constants
the copper winding is 11.7 % above its 293.15 K resistance
copper loss i^2*R(T) at the fixed point (17.9 W)
the hot winding slows the fan: 353.6 rad/s instead of 368.0 rad/s cold
the heat flow leaving the winding port is exactly the dissipated electrical power v*i of the heated resistor
first law of the winding: integral of the copper loss = C_w*(T_w - T_w0) + integral of the insulation heat flow (about 4e4 J pass through)
first law of the housing: insulation heat in = C_h*(T_h - T_h0) + convected heat out
Tellegen on the energetic ports (electrical and rotational); the thermal ports are pseudo-power (K*W) and are left out, the heated resistor inside Motor counts as dissipation
no solver failure, no connection, unit or causality error
